assumptions: Plants build to a rolling plan (demand signal + restore ~1.5 weeks of finished-goods cover), clipped by production-family line capacity then plant-wide capacity; executed quantity = plan x schedule adherence drawn uniformly in [0.90, 1.00].
Plant DCs are PUSHED stock by production; only RDCs and CDCs pull on a weekly (R,s,S) review with R = 1 week.

Lead times are drawn per order line from each lane's own mean and std in network_lanes.parquet, so every receipt arrives on its own realised transit rather than the average. The committed lead time quoted to the child is that lane's ~90th percentile.
CDC shortfalls are lost sales; PDC/RDC shortfalls backorder, following the fulfilment_type split in the dataset, which is clean by node type.
An internal replenishment order the parent cannot cover is cancelled, not backlogged; the child re-orders at the next weekly review.
A parent holds back its own expected demand for the remainder of the review period before releasing stock downstream, implementing 'customer orders served first'.

Routing comes from sku_sourcing_map.parquet, an input table derived from network structure: each RDC draws a SKU from the nearest plant DC whose plant is qualified to make it, and each CDC from its min-lead-time inbound RDC. It is not mined from simulated receipts.
Holding cost = (storage_cost_per_unit_year + carrying_pct x unit_cost) / 52, keyed on (dc_id, subcategory).
No shelf life, obsolescence or write-offs; no warehouse or lane capacity limits. Production capacity DOES bind.
Demand, lead-time and production RNG streams are independent, so two runs at the same seed differ only by the policy under test.

build_notes.demand_basis: forecast_qty x volume-weighted resampled forecast-error ratio

scenario.description: Southeast Beverages demand scales +25% for July 2026 (2026-W28..W31); MEIO plans for it, Twin simulates it; compare prepared vs unprepared vs baseline.

overrides.rationale: Planned +25% Southeast beverage demand in July (seasonal peak): "What if Southeast beverage demand rises 25% in July?" Assumptions recorded: magnitude exactly +25% (scale 1.25); window = the 4 ISO weeks whose Monday falls in July 2026 (2026-W28..W31, 2026-07-06 to 2026-08-02); scope = all Beverages SKUs at all Southeast DCs (100 SKUs across RDC02, RDC03, CDC03–CDC06, 397 demand lines); visibility = both sides (planner did not say whether the business sees it coming, so MEIO plans for it and the Twin simulates it; the unprepared arm already covers the surprise case). Pure volume surge: no price event, no volatility change, no capacity change.

details.hypothesis: A 25% July demand surge in Southeast Beverages will strain Southeast DC stock and PDC01 replenishment, lowering CDC/RDC fill rates in the unprepared arm; a prepared run (MEIO anticipates) recovers most of the lost service at the cost of higher inventory.
